rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will specially write the requested mercy for those who fulfill their duties and guard against disobedience and doubts.
rows.anchor: her türlü vazifelerini yapıp isyan ve şübühâttan korunacaklar.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditions sharply rebuke Moses’ people: unlike the present Israelites, they will not neglect piety and zakat through indifference, greed, or miserliness.
rows.anchor: Bu kayıtlarda kavm-i Mûsâ’ya mühim târizler vardır. Yani şimdiki seninkiler gibi takvâ ve zekâtı güçsünmeyecekler;

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised believers will maintain faith in the signs instead of repeating the Israelites’ cycles of belief and unbelief (4:137).
rows.anchor: ءَامَنُوا۟ ثُمَّ كَفَرُوا۟ ثُمَّ ءَامَنُوا۟ ثُمَّ كَفَرُوا۟ [en-Nisâ 4/137] televvününü göstermeyecekler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pious, zakat-giving believers are identified as those who follow the Messenger, the unlettered Prophet, in belief, speech, and action.
rows.anchor: Onlar o kimselerdir ki يَتَّبِعُونَ{}ٱلرَّسُولَ ٱلنَّبِىَّ ٱلْأُمِّىَّ O Resûl’e

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One proposed derivation of ummī relates it to ‘mother’: the Prophet remained in his original, unaltered natural state.
rows.anchor: “Ümm” nisbetidir ki “sanki anasından doğduğu hâl üzere kalmış, fıtrat-ı asliyesine kesb-i cedîd ile tegayyür ârız olmamış”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second proposed derivation relates ummī to the Arab community, known for not being skilled in calculation or writing.
rows.anchor: Ümmet-i Araba mensub demek olur ki [^4] إن َّا أُ َّمةٌ لاَ نَحْسبُ وَلاَ نَكْتُبُ mısdâkınca Araplar hesap ve kitap bilmez

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third proposed derivation makes ummī mean belonging to Umm al-Qurā, that is, Meccan.
rows.anchor: Ümmü’l-Kurâ’ya mensub, yani Mekkeli demektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All three derivations convey lack of reading and writing; ordinarily a deficiency, this Prophet’s divinely given knowledge beyond literate people is an innate perfection and a miracle proving his direct mission from God.
rows.anchor: bir ümmînin okuyup yazanlardan fazla âlim olması min tarafillah hilâf-ı âde olarak bilâ kesbin mevhub bir kemâl-i fıtrîye delâlet eder.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling him the unlettered Messenger and Prophet is an eloquent way to call his prophethood self-evident and miraculous.
rows.anchor: vasfı “o risâlet ve nübüvveti bedîhî, sâhib-i mucize” demenin daha belîğidir.

rows.speaker: Fuzûlî
rows.claim: Fuzuli’s couplet says that the Prophet’s knowledge while unlettered is sufficient proof of his truth.
rows.anchor: Nitekim Türk şâiri Fuzûlî bunu şu beytiyle anlatmıştır:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Contemporary People of the Book would find the Prophet written in Torah and Gospel and recognize him by name and attributes as readily as their own children (2:146); see also the account of Jacob (2:133).
rows.anchor: Tevrat ve İncil’de yazılmış bulacaklar. İsim ve evsâfıyla onun o olduğunda vicdanları şek etmeyecek يَعْرِفُونَهُۥ كَمَا يَعْرِفُونَ أَبْنَآءَهُمْ [el-Bakara 2/146]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God informed Moses at the meeting and in the Torah about the final Prophet, a mercy to all worlds, and promised the requested good for his community through following him; the Gospel would come after Torah and before Qur’an.
rows.anchor: Cenâb-ı Allah, Hazret-i Mûsâ’ya mîkātta ve Tevrat’ta rahmeten li’l-âlemîn olan Hâtemü’l-Enbiyâ’yı bildirmiş ve talep edilen rahmet ve hasenenin onun ümmeti için yazılacağını vaad

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At least by their attributes, Torah and Gospel contained the Messiah, the final Prophet, Gospel, Qur’an, and Criterion; learned People of the Book found that Moses’ people could gain the requested mercy only through following him (2:121).
rows.anchor: Tevrat ve İncil’de Hâtemü’l-Enbiyâ ve Kur’an, Furkan lâekal vasıflarıyla olsun muharrer ve mektub idi.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet commands recognized good—truth, justice, and what reason and revelation approve, summed up as reverence for God and compassion toward people—and forbids ugliness; enjoining good serves mercy while forbidding wrong removes causes of punishment.
rows.anchor: hakk u adli, akl ü naklin istihsan edeceği hayırlı şeyleri ki hulâsası Allah’ın emrine tâzim ve halkına şefkat

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet makes wholesome things lawful, especially good things previously forbidden to Moses’ people because of their wrongdoing, citing 4:160, 5:87, 2:168, 7:32, and 5:4.
rows.anchor: senin kavmine tahrim edilecek olan hoş ve temiz şeylerin hepsini- helâl ve meşrû kılacak لَا تُحَرِّمُوا۟ طَيِّبَٰتِ مَآ أَحَلَّ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمْ [el-Mâide 5/87]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No genuinely clean, pleasant food is forbidden unless impurity is mixed in, and enjoying natural wholesome things brings punishment only when accompanied by wasteful excess.
rows.anchor: hakikaten temiz ve leziz olan hiçbir şey, bir hubs karışmadıkça onlara haram olmayacak, israf ile inhimak edilmedikçe tayyibât-ı fıtriye ile intifâ‘sebeb-i ta‘zîb olmayacak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet forbids all physical impurities such as carrion, blood, pork, and wine, as well as moral wrongs such as gambling, usury, bribery, illicit gain, offerings to others, and violating others’ rights.
rows.anchor: Gerek meyte gerek dem, lahm-i hınzır, hamr vesâire gibi maddî habâset ile ve gerek kumar, ribâ, rüşvet ve suht

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Impurity causes punishment and pain, so the obligation of mercy requires avoiding it.
rows.anchor: habâset vaz‘-ı hakta sebeb-i azab ve âlâm olan şeyler olduğundan vücûb-ı rahmet bunlardan ictinâba mütevakkıftır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every forbidden thing has some impurity, while no genuinely wholesome thing is prohibited; this makes the resulting way of life a mercy worthy of gratitude.
rows.anchor: Herhangi bir cihetten bir hubsü bulunmayan hakīkī tayyibâtın hiçbiri tahrim edilmemek ve tahrim edilen şeylerin her hâlde bir habâseti bulunmak ne büyük rahmet

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The new law removes Israel’s burdensome duties, including the command to kill yourselves (2:54), and brings a lenient, easy, generous law free of constraint.
rows.anchor: اَنْفُسَكُمْ [^8] فَٱقْتُلُوٓا۟ [el-Bakara 2/54] gibi mükellef bulundukları ve altında ezilegeldikleri tekâlîf-i şâkkayı nesh edecek haracsız, yüsrlü, semâhatli bir şeriat getirecek.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All who believe in the unlettered Prophet, from any people, are included among his followers.
rows.anchor: yalnız senin kavminden değil, herhangi kavimden olursa olsun- bütün iman edenler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Honoring the Prophet means defending him against enemies; supporting him means serving the spread of the religion and application of its rulings.
rows.anchor: onu düşmanlarına karşı müdafaa ile tevkīr eyleyenler {وَنَصَرُوهُ} ve ona nasîr olanlar neşr-i din

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The light revealed with him is the Qur’an and also his Sunnah, life, commands, and prohibitions, which followers sincerely obey.
rows.anchor: hem onun nübüvvetiyle beraber getirdiği nûr-i Kur’ân’a, hem sünnet ve sîretine, emr ü nehyine cidden mutâva‘at edip

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only followers possessing all these qualities attain Moses’ requested mercy and worldly and otherworldly good, and definitively escape punishment.
rows.anchor: ancak o Nebiyy-i Ümmî’nin bütün bu evsâf ile muttasıf olan ashâb ve etbâ‘ıdır ki o senin yazılmasını istediğin rahmete

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised mercy is to be written for all people who meet these qualities, not just for Moses’ people.
rows.anchor: O rahmet, o hasene, o felah, şimdi bilhassa sizin için değil, ileride ale’l-umûm insanların duhûlüne müsait bu evsâf u şerâit

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s reply to Moses summarizes the opening of Baqara and echoes the declaration that the Lord has prescribed mercy for Himself (6:54).
rows.anchor: İşte Rabbi, Mûsâ’nın duasına Sûre-i Bakara’nın evvelindeki telhîse muntabık olan bu cevâbı verdi.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before Muhammad’s mission, encompassing mercy remained joined to the qualification that punishment strikes whom God wills, as a temporary or nonperpetual possibility.
rows.anchor: kaziyyesi عَذَابِىٓ أُصِيبُ بِهِۦ مَنْ أَشَآءُ ile müterâfık ve muhassas bir mutlaka-i vaktiyye veya mümkine-i lâ-dâime idi.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: From Muhammad’s mission onward, following him makes mercy a universal conditional obligation: God established a monotheistic universal law as the divinely required path to worldly and eternal mercy and escape from punishment.
rows.anchor: Bi‘set-i Muhammediyeden itibaren ise vasf-ı ittibâ‘şartıyla vâcib bir meşrûta-i âmme oldu. Yani kaziyye-i rahmet kaziyye-i azabdan fasl olunarak umum beşeriyet için

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those lacking this quality cannot be said to lose every possibility of mercy: punishment is certain for some, while particular mercy remains possible for others (39:53).
rows.anchor: diğer bazıları için de husûsî bir rahmet ihtimal dâhilindedir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses asked for this law of obligatory mercy particularly for himself and his people; God promised it for all by tying it to the final Prophet’s mission and people’s following of him.
rows.anchor: Mûsâ aleyhisselâm, bu vücûb-i rahmet şeriatını mîkāt-ı tevbede bilhassa kendisi ve kavmi için istemişti. Allah teâlâ da Resûl-i kül olan Âhir Zaman Peygamberi’nin bi‘setine ve ona ittibâ‘a ta‘lîk

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story of Moses and the preceding prophets culminates in the universal mercy-law and the promised mission of the final Prophet.
rows.anchor: mâsîka lehi ve hedef-i aksâsıdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The divine establishment over the Throne in 7:54 is manifested here: a hadith says time has returned to its original arrangement, and Muhammad’s era opens a new historical age of divinely ordered mercy, giving every people a universal path to salvation (1:7).
rows.anchor: asr-ı Muhammedî’den itibaren zaman, edvâr-ı mâziyesine bir nihâyet veriyor ve istivâ-yı rahmânî ile yepyeni bir devr-i tarih açıyor

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise in Torah and Gospel shows that Moses was not a universal messenger but directed the Israelites toward the final Prophet; Moses’ story now commands proclamation of Muhammad’s universal mission.
rows.anchor: İmdi Tevrat ve İncil’in muhtevî olduğu o beyân-ı va‘d karşısında Mûsâ aleyhisselâm’ın resûl-i kül olmadığı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Turkish rendering presents the primordial testimony as God making people witnesses against themselves and asking whether He is their Lord.
rows.anchor: onları nefislerine karşı şâhid tutarak “Rabbiniz değil miyim?” diye işhâd ettiği vakit

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The descendants’ excuse is rendered as blaming those who established falsehood, then asking whether they will be destroyed for the corrupters’ acts.
rows.anchor: ancak önceden atalarımız şirk koştular, biz ise onlardan sonra bir zürriyet idik

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The translation says the signs are elaborated so that people may return.
rows.anchor: Ve işte biz âyetleri böyle tafsil ediyoruz ve gerektir ki rücû‘etsinler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rendered account portrays a person who slipped away from God’s signs and then followed Satan into misguidance.
rows.anchor: ona âyetlerimizi sormuştuk da o, onlardan sıyrıldı çıktı. Derken onu şeytan arkasına taktı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The translation renders attachment to the earth as sinking into lowliness and describes the denier through the dog that pants whether approached or left alone.
rows.anchor: o, yere (alçaklığa) saplandı ve hevâsının ardına düştü. Artık onun meseli o köpeğin meseline benzer

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those whom God leaves astray are rendered as the ones who fall into loss.
rows.anchor: kimi de dalâlete bırakırsa hüsrâna düşenler de işte onlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The translation says many jinn and humans were created for Hell; lacking understanding, sight, and hearing, they are like livestock, even more bewildered, and heedless.
rows.anchor: Onların öyle kalbleri vardır ki onlarla duymazlar ve öyle gözleri vardır ki onlarla görmezler ve öyle kulakları vardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rendering instructs people to invoke God by His most beautiful names and leave those who deviate regarding them to their coming recompense.
rows.anchor: Allah’ındır en güzel isimler (esmâ-i hüsnâ) onun için siz O’na onlarla çağırın ve O’nun isimlerinde sapıklık eden mülhidleri bırakın

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final rendering mentions a community among God’s creatures that guides by truth and acts justly through it.
rows.anchor: bizim halk ettiklerimizden bir ümmet de var ki hakka rehberlik ederler ve onunla icrâ-yı adalet eylerler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every human descendant is given a valid human nature capable of witnessing, and an innate covenant to recognize God’s oneness and lordship; the verse invokes God’s testimony in 3:18.
rows.anchor: her zürriyetin üzerinde fıtraten böyle bir taahhüd bulunduğuna

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human self-awareness and possession of spirit and consciousness entail accepting God’s lordship and unity; one’s own existence bears witness to God.
rows.anchor: kendimizi duymanın kendi varlığımızın Senin vücûb-i vücûduna, vahdâniyetine, rubûbiyetine bir şâhid bulunduğunu şu‘ûr-ı sarih ile duymuyorduk.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God recalled the otherwise hidden covenant clearly so that people could not excuse themselves at Judgment by claiming they were unaware or had received no explicit reminder.
rows.anchor: Hafî olan bu taahhüdü bize sarâhaten tezkir ve iş‘âr lütfunda da bulunmadın diye

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Descendants cannot excuse shirk by blaming their ancestors or claiming helpless ignorance and inherited guilt; each person was independently formed and made self-aware, so each answers for their own covenant and sin.
rows.anchor: sizler babalarınızın cürmünden, babalarınızın taahhüdünden değil, kendi insanlık taahhüdünüzden ve kendi cürmünüzden mes’ul olacaksınız.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each descendant was separated from the father’s loins, given an individual nature and agency, and made a direct witness to God’s address, but failed to testify and turned to shirk.
rows.anchor: Evvelâ zürriyetler babalarının sulbünden alındı, çıkarıldı ayrıldı, onlardan ayrı bir fıtrat ve fiil verildi.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God details the signs to turn blind imitators of falsehood back to truth, and the Messenger is to remind them.
rows.anchor: o bâtıl mukallidleri hakka- dönsünler diyedir ki yaparız.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person in the parable had been given divine signs and possessed scholarly or religious standing, but stripped himself of them and let Satan lead him astray.
rows.anchor: ona âyetlerimizi vermiştik -ilmî, dînî haysiyeti vardı- onlardan sıyrıldı çıktı da

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God could have raised him by the signs, but he clung to worldly life or abasement and followed desire; divine will did not elevate him, and he was left to himself in his fall.
rows.anchor: sefalete meyletti ve hevâsına uydu da o âyetlerden sıyrıldı, dinden çıktı, sukūt etti

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports identify the figure either as Balaam ibn Eber or the Canaanite Balaam ibn Baura, a learned Israelite whose accepted prayers turned toward worldly interests and support for tyrants against Moses or Joshua.
rows.anchor: Bunun Mûsâ aleyhisselâm zamanında Benî İsrâil ulemâsından Bel‘am b. Ebr veya Ken‘ânîlerden Bel‘am b. Bâûrâ nâmında birisi olduğuna

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report connects the revelation to Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt, who read earlier scriptures, expected a prophet, hoped to be that prophet himself, and rejected Muhammad from envy.
rows.anchor: Ümeyye b. Ebü’s-Salt da bazı kütüb-i ilâhiye okumuş ve bir peygamber geleceğine kanaat hâsıl etmiş ve onun kendisi olması ümidinde bulunurmuş.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı suggests the underlying story may be Balaam’s while Umayya is the occasion of revelation, but says the Qur’an aims to portray the person’s condition rather than identify him.
rows.anchor: Diyebiliriz ki asıl kıssa, Bel‘am veya Bel‘am’ın olduğu hâlde sebeb-i nüzûl Ümeyye olmuştur. Fakat Kur’an şunu gösteriyor ki kıssadan maksad şahsın târifi değil, hâlini tefhim ve temsildir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dog’s relentless panting whether driven or left alone symbolizes the lowest degree of a fall: it never escapes distress, and panting is the dog’s uniquely base state.
rows.anchor: yorsan da dilini uzatır solur, rahat ettirsen de dilini uzatır solur, hiçbir zaman ıztırabdan kurtulmaz.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parable applies to people who deny God’s signs, identified as the Jewish community that inherited scripture but pursued low worldly gain (7:169); their state resembles those unaffected by warning (2:6).
rows.anchor: İşte bu mesel âyetlerimizi tekzib eden o kavmin meselidir ki خَلْفٌۭ وَرِثُوا۟ ٱلْكِتَٰبَ يَأْخُذُونَ عَرَضَ هَٰذَا ٱلْأَدْنَىٰ [el-A‘râf 7/169] olan kavm-i cehûddur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Messenger is to recount the story in hope that some listeners will reflect and be awakened, while keeping that possibility in view.
rows.anchor: Binâen‘aleyh bu kıssayı naklet ki belki bir düşünürler içlerinde mütenebbih olacaklar bulunur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Denying the signs is an ugly example of people wronging themselves; Elmalılı asks whether those with even partial awareness will reflect on their shameful state.
rows.anchor: Kendilerine cüz’î şuuru olanlar, kendilerinin bu çirkin hâllerini, bu çirkin mesellerini bir kere düşünüp de utanmaz mı?
